Euro NCAP Hails the Return of the Buttons, but It's an Anomaly Rather Than the New Normal
11 photos
Photo: Euro NCAP
Two years ago, Euro NCAP declared war on the touchscreen-heavy user interfaces. The 2026 testing procedures mandate physical controls for basic functions to promote traffic safety. However, only European and Korean carmakers have aligned with this requirement. In contrast, other carmakers have continued to bet on touchscreen controls.
The latest Euro NCAP test round appears to validate the agency's strategy of penalizing touchscreen-centric user interfaces in new vehicles. The safety body released its latest test results, claiming that physical buttons for basic functions are making a comeback in new vehicle models. Euro NCAP pointed to the Audi Q7 and Kia EV2 as good examples, while the Xpeng X9 was bashed as still relying on a touchscreen interface.
The former two models that the Euro NCAP tested in its latest round appear to validate the agency's stance that touchscreen controls distract drivers' attention and thus compromise safety. Audi was given as an example of a carmaker that reversed its position regarding touchscreen controls. It previously ditched physical buttons, but has reversed course and has now scored a high 90% for driving controls in the latest tests.
The Audi Q7 uses buttons and stalks that are clearly visible and ergonomically positioned, reducing the chances of driver distraction. The Kia EV2, evaluated during the same round, follows a similar path. Like its Korean sister-brand Hyundai, Kia believes that physical controls should be kept at least for the most usual vehicle functions.
While the Audi Q7 and the Kia EV2 represent two opposing market segments, they are not representative of the European car market in general. Many other vehicles sold in Europe don't quite observe Euro NCAP's recommendations, and there's not much the safety agency can do about it.
Photo: Audi The Xpeng X9, also tested during this round, follows Tesla user interface philosophy. This means that it relies heavily on its central touchscreen for core functions, with not many buttons to speak of. Euro NCAP thinks this could lead to driver distraction, which is why it rewarded the MPV a low 20% score for its primary driving controls. That didn't change the overall result, with the Xpeng X9 still receiving the same 5-star award as the Audi Q7 and the Kia EV2.
While I agree that physical buttons are a better option than touchscreen controls, I don't think buttons have a future. And not because touchscreens are ubiquitous in new vehicles, but because there are better options than both buttons and touchscreen controls. Rivian was right that voice controls are the future, and now Tesla has proven that talking to your car is a much better solution than fiddling with controls, regardless of their type.
The Grok assistant in Tesla EVs can now control a wide range of vehicle functions, including infotainment, navigation, and climate. These are, coincidentally, the same functions that Kia, Hyundai, and Audi have reserved physical buttons for. Other carmakers are also using AI assistants to control basic functions of their vehicles. Considering all this, Euro NCAP's stubbornness to penalize touchscreen controls seems like an anachronism.

It’s about the size of the Kia PV5 and VW ID. Buzz. As “a real alternative to SUVs and saloons,” Renault’s E-Space Concept makes you want to love minivans again.
Renault reveals the E-Space Concept, an electric MPV
While minivans aren’t the first thing that comes to mind when you think of a “cool” or fun-to-drive vehicle, Renault is out to change that.
Renault unveiled the E-Space Concept at the Paris Motor Show on Monday, a modern-day take on its iconic minivan from the 80s.
Although it’s still a concept, the MPV is designed as an electric successor to the original Renault Espace from 1984.

With an MPV-body style and open layout, Renault said the minivan offers “a real alternative to SUVs and saloons” that dominate the market.
The E-Space Concept measures 4,700 mm long, 2,020 mm wide, and 1,670 mm tall, or about the size of the Kia PV5 Passenger and VW ID. Buzz short-wheelbase (SWB). While it retains a similar design to the first Espace, the electric version features a modern twist.
Renault E-Space Concept (Source: Renault)
Designed to maximize efficiency, the concept sits lower than a traditional SUV, with smooth lines and a roof spoiler reminiscent of the Espace 2 and 3.
Inside, the designers created a fully glazed cabin inspired by Bauhaus architecture, and in particular, German-American architect Ludwig Mies van der Rohe.
As such, the glass roof and windows extend well beyond the already low waistline. With the low waistline, “you can see into the cabin when standing next to the car. And once again, you can drive with your elbows on the door,” said Romain Gauvin, Renault Brand Head of Advanced Design & Concept Cars.
Renault E-Space Concept (Source: Renault)
The double-hinged rear doors open to a spacious interior with six individual seats and a flat-floor design.
Inspired by the original 1984 Espace, the seats break free from the traditional bucket design with “lacquered shells ” that appear to be floating.
Renault E-Space Concept interior (Source: Renault)
Each seat can rotate. The second-row seats can swivel 180 degrees to create a “TGV train square” with the third row. Passengers in the second row have a standard folding tray table and a 12.3″ screen mounted on the headrests.
In the four-seat configuration, where the second-row seats fold, you can create a large table with a remote-control console.
Renault E-Space Concept interior (Source: Renault)
The console includes an air purifier, a small fridge, video game controllers, and last but not least, a game of Connect 4.
Ambient lighting runs across the cabin, while night lights are built into the speakers. Reading lights are also mounted on the rail in the center of the glass roof.
The concept features a massive pillar-to-pillar curved display, OpenR Panorama, plus a center infotainment screen. Both can swivel around a base behind the steering wheel.
Speaking of which, the compact steering wheel design features steer-by-wire technology that’s “free from all the physical constraints typically associated with steering,” according to Stéphane Maiore, Renault Brand Head of Interior Design.
Renault didn’t confirm whether or when we will see a production version of the E-Space , but hinted that it’s a “contemporary retake on travel and family mobility in the electric age” and “outlines its vision for the car of the future.”

This Is a One-Owner 1964 1/2 Mustang Convertible, and Fate Has Been So Cruel to It
114 photos
Photo: Flashback Enterprises Inc on eBay
A mix of good news and bad news. That’s what you’ll be getting if you stick around for a few more minutes to discover this 1964 1/2 Mustang convertible. The car is here because it needs a second chance, begging for restoration on eBay, where the owner listed it for sale.
The owner is realistic and admits that in addition to serving as a restoration project, this Mustang is so rough that it can also be used for parts. Despite being a 1964 1/2 Mustang, all parts would also fit a 1965 sibling.
In fact, the 1964 1/2 Mustangs don’t exist officially. They are just early 1965 models, so except for generators and alternators, the two models are identical mechanical-wise. Ford operated some changes in the engine lineup when the 1965 model year officially came to be, introducing a new six and replacing the base V8 choice.
It’s no secret that the Mustang was a hit from the first day of availability.Ford received no more, no less than 22,000 orders on the first day alone, so when the 1965 Mustang was released officially in mid-August, the carmaker had already received 120,000 cars.
The Mustang wasn’t necessarily an expensive car, and the base hardtop, which was fitted with a six-cylinder engine and a 3-speed manual transmission, could be had for only $2,320. The convertible was a bit more expensive at $2,557. For eventually launched a 2+2 fastback in September to help the entire lineup reach final sales of 680,989 units in its first year on the market.
The Mustang was originally sold with a 170ci six-cylinder unit rated at 105 horsepower. This engine was dropped when the 1965 Mustang was officially ready. A 200ci six with 120 horsepower became the standard unit on six-cylinder configurations.
The base V8 on 1964 1/2 Mustangs was a 260ci unit with a two-barrel configuration. This engine also got the ax when the 1965 model year received the green light, and a 289 with a two-barrel carburetor became the base V8 with 200 horsepower.
A four-barrel version - which was also offered on early models, but with upgraded power now - was available as an option with 225 horsepower. The top choice was the HiPo configuration that produced over 270 horsepower.
This Mustang is fitted with a 289ci engine and an automatic transmission. This should, at least theoretically, be good news for someone who wants to restore the car to day-one specifications without losing the original goodies.
This is a one-owner car, and considering so many documents are available, you should be able to check all numbers quite easily. This means it shouldn’t take long to figure out if the engine is original, and for a restoration guy, this is big news.
On the other hand, the engine isn’t by any means in good shape. “The engine is stuck from sitting,” the seller says, unfortunately without sharing more specifics. There’s a chance this car has been parked for decades, possibly even outside, judging from the rust damage we can see in the pictures.
While I’ve seen cars in worse shape getting a second chance, I believe this Mustang is worth an in-person inspection. There’s a lot of rust damage on the cars, and hats off to the seller for posting such a large photo gallery.
I don’t believe this Mustang should be used for parts for a very simple reason: it’s a one-owner specimen that still has the original documents, including the original title, loan approval, and bill of sale. These make the Mustang more of a collectible, despite not being exactly a rare car.
The convertible body style is also a solid selling point because most of the cars that were sold initially were hardtops. The convertible top still works and goes up and down, but the seller says it comes with a few holes caused by mice.
The selling price makes perfect sense for this car. The owner is realistic and knows that saving this Mustang not only will involve a lot of work but will also eat up more money, especially in terms of metalwork.
The engine also isn’t working, so anyone who wants to save it for the sake of keeping the car original will have to spend additional dollars to get it up and running.
That is why $5,000 looks like a fair price. However, the owner also enabled the Make Offer option on eBay, meaning that buyers who want the car but don’t want to pay that much can easily send their offers through the auction platform. The listing expires in just one day, but there is a chance that the Mustang will be relisted in the coming weeks if it fails to find a new home.
The car is parked in Imlay City, Michigan, and will obviously need transportation to your garage.

GA-ASI’s Mojave STOL supports airfields without airports, allowing soldiers to find, track, and eliminate adversaries using improvised launch and recovery sites.
A new, more challenging operational environment means the U.S. Army must field platforms that generate strategic advantages while conducting missions from the tactical edge.
Today’s battlefield is contested across all domains. The proliferation of low-cost, effective systems, as well as high-tech munitions, long-range missiles, and advanced air defenses, means platforms must operate effectively in denied conditions without imposing unsustainable costs or maintenance demands.
General Atomics Aeronautical Systems, Inc. (GA-ASI) offers two aircraft tailored to the Army’s need to operate in this threat environment, with the flexibility to adapt as those needs evolve: the Mojave Short Takeoff and Landing (STOL) aircraft and the Gray Eagle® 25M .
Although the aircraft share elements of the Gray Eagle family, they are optimized for different operational challenges.
Mojave STOL is designed to deliver expeditionary access from austere locations, while Gray Eagle 25M offers the endurance and range necessary for the Pacific theater, along with the payload capacity to support the Army’s multi-domain operations concept.
Bringing Aviation Closer to the Mission
Mojave STOL is designed for missions where runways are undesirable, unavailable, damaged, or vulnerable. Its STOL capability enables operations from unimproved surfaces, including roads and dirt tracks, as well as from amphibious vessels.
Runway independence expands commanders’ options in remote or contested areas. The aircraft can operate closer to distributed forces, take on fuel and munitions at austere locations, and return to the fight without relying on airfield infrastructure.
This approach reflects an enduring operational lesson: in demanding environments, rugged, reliable, and plentiful platforms can provide an advantage over systems that are more complex, expensive, or difficult to maintain.
Mojave STOL provides options for overwhelming mass at the right time and place while retaining key sensor and payload capabilities and supporting long-range, persistent mission profiles.
While modern electric and vertical-lift concepts offer tactical flexibility, their high unit costs, mechanical complexity, undetermined supply chain security, and maintenance burdens present challenges for sustained expeditionary operations driving cost, manpower, and risk.
Mojave STOL is built around a straightforward, time-tested aircraft, a proven design, and an established production and sustainment philosophy, enabling the flexibility to move with expeditionary forces while avoiding complex infrastructure demands.
Its ability to operate from smaller naval vessels also creates potential applications for maritime, contested logistics, and special operations missions.
Modernizing Gray Eagle for Contested Operations
Gray Eagle 25M is an extensively modernized version of the MQ-1C Gray Eagle, designed to support long-endurance missions in complex threat environments. Its roles include persistent, real-time threat detection/identification and support for long-range targeting operations.
A central feature of the aircraft is its Modular Open Systems Approach (MOSA) architecture.
MOSA uses defined interfaces and modular components to help integrate new technologies more quickly and affordably. This open architecture approach is intended to help the Army respond to changing threats while reducing the time and cost associated with future upgrades.
Another significant improvement comes in the form of the expeditionary laptop-based ground control station and ground support equipment. This portable system eliminates the need for large, containerized GCS satellite systems, transport vehicles, and ground support equipment, reducing equipment weight by 130,000 pounds per platoon.
Combined with the new, more powerful turbo-diesel Heavy Fuel Engine (HFE) 2.0, these improvements reduce field service representative and soldier workload while increasing maintenance-free operational periods, with a sustainment cost savings of roughly $200 million annually.
Gray Eagle 25M delivers critical RSTA capabilities for a decisive battlefield advantage.
The EagleEye® multi-mode radar , for example, is designed to provide substantially greater range than legacy systems, with an increase of up to five times.
Together, these capabilities support Gray Eagle 25M’s mission to maintain persistent awareness and contribute to decision-making in high-threat environments.
Complementary Aircraft for the Army
The two aircraft offer the Army a complementary range of capabilities.
Mojave STOL is optimized for expeditionary access, operational flexibility, and runway-independent operations in regions such as the Indo-Pacific, where forces cannot count on reliable access to paved runways.
Gray Eagle 25M is optimized for endurance, sensing, processing, and survivability in contested environments. Its advanced sensor suite, combined with tactics refined through millions of hours of combat operations by Gray Eagle and other GA-ASI aircraft, enables the platform to operate over long distances and remain effective in high-threat conditions.
Both aircraft are designed to evolve as threats and mission requirements change.
Gray Eagle 25M and Mojave’s open architecture support the integration of new capabilities, helping maintain relevance across different areas of operation. What’s more, they cover the full breadth of conflict, from peacetime to large-scale combat operations, with adaptable, responsive, critical capability.
Mojave STOL can likewise accommodate expanded payload options, including electronic warfare systems and air-launched effects.
Investing in Scalable Capability
Mojave STOL conducts short-field operations from a rough maneuver trail during a demonstration with Hanwha Aerospace in South Korea on September 16, 2026.
GA-ASI has made manufacturing and engineering investments intended to support continued modernization and larger-scale production.
Collaboration with Hanwha Aerospace is expanding production facilities and research and development activities, helping create the infrastructure needed to support scalable output.
The partnership is aimed at advancing Mojave STOL’s capabilities while supporting more affordable production. That means the Army will not necessarily have to choose between capability and mass.
In addition, GA-ASI’s existing millions of square feet of manufacturing infrastructure, skilled in-house workforce, and available capacity position the company to begin building and delivering aircraft today.
By choosing Gray Eagle 25M and Mojave STOL, the Army would be investing in mature, adaptable capabilities designed for rapid delivery and scalable employment.
Visitors to GA-ASI’s Booth 6619 at the Association of the United States Army’s Annual Meeting and Exposition can discuss with experts how these systems are prepared to support Army operations in today’s high-threat environments and adapt to the challenges ahead.

Freight fraud can leave victims wondering whether anyone else has faced the same attack. Stolen identities, deceptive pickups and double brokering can strike businesses across transportation. Many companies never publicly discuss what happened afterward. Freight Fraud Awareness Day wants to change that.
Freight Fraud Awareness Day returns Oct. 14 with advocates across transportation and insurance. This year’s campaign focuses on education, awareness and advocacy. Organizers encourage open dialogue about criminal schemes, industry impacts and available prevention resources. Verified Carrier, Truckstop, Northland Insurance, Travelers, GenLogs, FreightValidate and Freight Bites support the effort.
Andrey Drotenko, president of strategic relations at Verified Carrier, discussed the campaign in a September interview with FreightWaves. “It’s a moment to slow down, compare notes, and just act together,” Drotenko explained. Participants can discuss incidents without revealing safeguards criminals might exploit. That approach allows useful intelligence to circulate while protecting sensitive procedures.
This marks the third annual Freight Fraud Awareness Day. FreightWaves covered the inaugural campaign in October 2024 . Early efforts focused on building awareness around transportation scams. Organizers plan new opportunities for professionals to share expertise in coming years.
‘It’s not just me’
Drotenko compared fraud victims with friends discovering they share similar struggles. Another person might reveal an experience that suddenly feels familiar. “Oh, it’s not just me,” he recalled. That realization reflects the campaign’s push for more open dialogue across transportation.
Gary Thomas, manager of risk and mitigation at SPG Cargo & Logistics, has watched criminal tactics evolve. Traditional offenders once needed physical proximity to targeted freight. Digital tools now allow identity manipulation from almost anywhere. Modern security providers must counter methods that barely existed a decade ago.
“We went from a traditional bad guy waiting at the truck stop,” Thomas explained. Criminals can now “digitally manipulate somebody’s identity and the supply chain.” Technology has changed the threat facing commercial transportation. “By working together we hope to bridge that gap.”
Criminal methods keep changing
Retired Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Detective Gerardo Pachuca has watched offenders exploit transportation knowledge. “Cargo theft has been exploding,” Pachuca explained. Some criminals understand legitimate operations before turning that experience against businesses. “They know how to exploit and misuse those loopholes on the dark side of the industry.”
Federal investigators are seeing similar threats. The FBI’s Memphis Cargo Theft Task Force has warned that cyber-enabled schemes allow criminals to identify valuable shipments before arriving for pickup. Those tactics demonstrate how deception can turn legitimate freight movements into theft opportunities.
Chuck Forsaith, vice president of the Pharmaceutical Cargo Security Coalition , has witnessed another shift. Earlier cases often involved thieves physically taking merchandise. Modern schemes increasingly rely on deception instead. Pharmaceutical losses create additional risks when stolen products return to legitimate commerce.
“Back then it was almost exclusively what we would call straight theft,” Forsaith explained. Today’s methods depend more heavily on some form of fraud. Criminals may ignore required quality controls after taking pharmaceutical products. “That can significantly impact the integrity of the products once they are reintroduced into a supply chain.”
Freight Fraud Awareness Day gives transportation professionals an opportunity to bring those experiences into the open. Companies can discuss what happened without exposing every security measure protecting their operations. Those accounts may reveal threats another business has never encountered. They can also remind victims of something much simpler.
It’s not just me.
Why It Matters
Criminals benefit when fraud stays hidden. Sharing real incidents can expose patterns, close information gaps and help stop the same scheme from hitting someone else.
CFCO
In my opinion, awareness matters most when professionals know what to do next. The FreightWaves Certified Fraud Compliance Officer course turns fraud prevention into a repeatable verification process. Training helps teams question inconsistencies, recognize warning signs and make stronger decisions before freight moves. A consistent approach can stop one overlooked detail from becoming an expensive loss.

source_document.body:
The Port of Los Angeles handled a record 1,042,652 twenty-foot equivalent units in September, marking the busiest month in its 118-year history as rising imports helped cap unprecedented quarterly and four-month cargo totals.
Throughput exceeded the previous monthly record, set in July 2025, by more than 20,000 TEUs. The port handled nearly 3 million TEUs from July through September, its busiest quarter, and nearly 4 million TEUs from June through September, its strongest four-month stretch .
Volumes that reflected an extended peak season on reliable demand defied economic uncertainty, rising interest rates, chaotic tariff policy, and assorted geopolitics.
Loaded imports reached 545,696 TEUs in September, up 19% from a year earlier. Loaded exports increased 10% to 125,751 TEUs, while empty-container volume totaled approximately 371,206 TEUs, the highest monthly total in port history.
Through the first nine months of 2026, Los Angeles handled nearly 8.1 million TEUs, more than 3% ahead of the same period a year ago.
Port Executive Director Gene Seroka in a media briefing attributed the cargo surge to resilient consumer demand , inventory replenishment and shippers allocating more freight to Los Angeles amid challenges along other global trade routes.
“September was a month for the record books, and it was part of an extraordinary run for the Port of Los Angeles,” Seroka said.
Seroka said tariffs had fallen from levels seen earlier this year, providing importers with greater cost certainty and allowing them to replenish inventories. He also cited continued consumer spending and challenges along the Suez and Panama Canal routes as contributors to the record cargo run.
Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass said the port’s performance reinforced its role as a local and national economic engine. She praised Seroka’s leadership and members of the International Longshore and Warehouse Union for their work handling the cargo.
“Los Angeles is strong because our Port is strong, and none of this would be possible without our talented, dedicated , and skilled workforce,” Bass said.

This 1984 Beaver Is a Low-Mileage Motorhome With a Full Bedroom and Skylight Shower
18 photos
Photo: Facebook Marketplace/TJ Cameron
When it comes to classic motorhomes, we often think about rigs built by Winnebago , Airstream, and Travco. Beaver Motorcoach Corporation, for instance, is mostly unknown outside the official, but it produced some impressive RVs back in the day.
Beaver was founded in 1968 by Jim Hogue and Frank Storch. It was named after the Oregon State University mascot and started out by building slide-in campers for pickup trucks. It joined the motorhome market in 1974, initially with Class C vehicles. These were built on Chevrolet and Dodge chassis and powered by big-block V8 engines.
In the early 1980s, Beaver began making Class A motorhomes. It also introduced diesel engines around the same time. Unfortunately, the company struggled financially later in the decade and had to file for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in late 1993.
Beaver was purchased by Safari Motorcoach Corporation following the bankruptcy, which in turn was bought by Monaco Coach in 2002. The name disappeared in 2009 after Monaco went bankrupt and was purchased by Navistar International .
The Beaver 40 you see here was built in 1984. The 40-foot motorhome is the company's largest vehicle and was fitted with features that were considered luxurious at the time. The camper surfaced in Brandon, South Dakota, and appears to be an unrestored survivor with only 15,500 original miles (24,945 km) on the odometer.
The motorhome sports Beaver's typical 1980s livery, which included dark red and brown stripes over a cream background. The weathering is consistent with an unrestored vehicle that's been carefully maintained. I don't think that this camper spent a lot of time under full exposure to the elements.
The interior is in even better condition. I'd even go as far as to call it pristine, but you will notice some light weathering here and there. The vehicle includes a full rear master bedroom with a closet, a full bathroom with a large shower, a refrigerator, a freezer, a microwave, and even a built-in ice maker. It has dual kitchen sinks, lots of storage room, and two TVs.
The vehicle was equipped with a backup camera, and the seller says that it still works. It also has a fancy horn that can play 50 different songs. The front compartment includes two captain's chairs, both still wearing the original upholstery, which appears to be sound.
This Beaver was born right after the company began using diesel engines. The 40-foot motorhome draws juice from a Caterpillar 3208 engine, displacing a massive 10.4 liters. The V8 was introduced in the 1970s and was available in various configurations. There's no info on whether this one is naturally aspirated or turbocharged.
The all-motor units delivered between 150 and 210 horsepower, while the turbocharged variants generated up to 320 horsepower. Assuming it has a turbo (due to the massive curb weight), this Beaver should have at least 250 horsepower on tap. The drivetrain runs properly thanks to recent maintenance.
Although it may not be iconic or even very desirable, this Beaver is a solid option if you want a large vintage motorhome that doesn't break the bank. Speaking of which, the seller wants $12,000 to let it go. What's your take on this sticker?

1969 Dodge Coronet Charger SuperbeeRd Is a Shocker That'll Make You Weep, or Throw Cash at It
24 photos
Photo: Facebook Marketplace/Timofey Kosharnyy
1969 Dodge Charger Daytona, 1970 Plymouth Road Runner Superbird. End of Mopar aero warriors story. The two monikers have a special place within the sacred realms of Detroit. Say what you will, but there’s nothing like those two. Unless, of course, we take this red “WTF” (What the Fantasy) into consideration. Which is all of the above, combined into one. One of None.
Chrysler Corporation didn’t just add a new chapter to automotive history books in 1969-1970, when its two racing divisions, Dodge and Plymouth, released the mythical winged warriors. No, good ol’ Ma Mopar kicked the doors of imagination wide open, and let loose all the demons that inhabited the most secluded corners of fantasy, giving them a license to roam free wherever they wished. As it turned out, the little satans decided to play the NASCAR theme for Halloween.
The Dodge Charger and the Plymouth Road Runner were already megahits in the late sixties, so it was only natural that ChryCo would use those platforms to homologate the aerodynamic nose and wing for the high banks of the National Association for Stock Car Auto Racing. Built strictly to meet homologation numbers, the two models were acquired tastes at first, and are now holy grails worth a lot of cash. Think millions, in certain cases. American dollars’ worth of millions.
Then again, reality is that a universally acknowledged truth is the one that says gearheads who simply cannot afford a genuine winged Mopar (which is frankly most of them) will sometimes settle for the next best thing. No, I’m not talking about the base, generic, commonplace model (Charger or Road Runner). I’m talking about replicas.
Photo: Facebook Marketplace/Timofey Kosharnyy Building or buying a tribute car is a perfectly fine compromise. There are plenty of beautifully executed homages out there roaring up and down the streets. These faithful recreations often bring immense honor and well-deserved pride to their dedicated automotive passionate builders. And then, there’s this… (insert noun, adjective, or whatever part of speech you deem fitting).
The particular vehicle we are examining today is so wildly off the charts that describing it won’t suffice a mere complete rewriting of the automotive rule books. No, you might need a chaotic collision of multiple cinematic universes to even begin making sense of it. Ladies and gentlemen, behold the magnificent absurdity of the 1969 Dodge Charger Coronet SuperbeeRd. The WHAT, you ask? Yes, you read that absolute nonsense perfectly correctly.
It perfectly mirrors my almost exact thought when I first stumbled upon this listing. I will freely admit there may or may not have been several loud religious blasphemes uttered when I read the descriptions. I am a heathen and a pagan and an infidel, and also fairly certain I invoked the guy down under - and his entire army of horned and hooved havoc raisers - trying to comprehend the sheer audacity of this bizarre rolling identity crisis machine.
Photo: Facebook Marketplace/Timofey Kosharnyy I now, it’s 2026, and self-identification doesn’t live constrained in the cufflinks of that “0” and “1” duality, so this brow-raising jaw-dropper has a place here. But the mind absolutely boggles at the thought process behind this build. Why would anyone decide to build a Plymouth Superbird out of a Dodge?
More confusingly, why build it out of a 1969 car, and specifically out of a Coronet? If they started out with a Dodge chassis anyway, why on earth would they not simply create a 1969 Dodge Charger Daytona tribute to keep things somewhat historically accurate?
Instead of logic, we get this magnificent red monstrosity. We are looking at a 1969 Dodge Coronet proudly wearing a 1970 Plymouth Superbird body kit. This automotive Frankenstein is currently roaming the deepest, darkest corners of the internet, desperately screaming for attention. The seller has generously plastered it across multiple platforms, ensuring maximum visibility for a build that leaves purists weeping quietly into their greasy shop rags.
Photo: Facebook Marketplace/Timofey Kosharnyy Consistency is clearly not a priority for whoever unleashed this creation upon the world. The vehicle has been listed in three different places, namely Craigslist, Facebook Marketplace, and ClassicCars.com. Remarkably, it goes by a completely different name depending on which digital billboard you happen to be viewing. It is almost as if the car is currently in the witness protection program and needs a steady supply of fresh fake aliases.
Over on Facebook Marketplace, it nonchalantly poses as a 1969 Dodge Charger. Meanwhile, the listing on ClassicCars.com finally admits the truth, calling it a 1969 Dodge Coronet. However, the Craigslist advertisement gets the most brilliantly chaotic moniker of them all. There, it is proudly heralded as the 1969 Dodge Coronet SuperBeeRd. This linguistic masterpiece perfectly captures the utter confusion radiating from every single inch of its modified bodywork today.
The pricing strategy is equally baffling and seems entirely dependent on your chosen shopping venue. If you fancy buying this unique machine through ClassicCars.com, you must be prepared to part with $75,000. Conversely, if you prefer braving the wild and unpredictable frontiers of Facebook Marketplace or Craigslist, the asking price suddenly drops to a somewhat more reasonable $69,000.
Photo: Facebook Marketplace/Timofey Kosharnyy Cryptocurrency is also enthusiastically accepted for this completely bizarre financial endeavor, but I’m willing to bet an entire pint of gasoline that the owner might be open to doubloons, tetradrachms, sesterces, denars, or shillings – as long as they’re pure mint silver or gold, it’s fair game.
Then there is the absolutely fascinating mystery of the odometer readings. According to the laconic Craigslist description, this custom project has covered a mere 150 miles since its unholy resurrection. That is certainly not too shabby for a supposedly fresh build sporting a clean title and current registration extending through April 2027. One might assume the car basically just rolled straight out of the garage and onto the pavement outside.
However, the ClassicCars.com listing confidently claims the vehicle has only traveled 90 miles. To make matters even more convoluted, the Facebook Marketplace post proudly states it has been driven 1,000 miles. Perhaps the car sneaks out and drives itself while the owner sleeps. Alternatively, keeping track of actual distance is just another boring rule this one-of-none NASCAR tribute has boldly and proudly chosen to ignore.
Photo: Facebook Marketplace/Timofey Kosharnyy The descriptions themselves are hilariously laconic for such an enormous build. We are bluntly informed it features a 440 engine paired with a 727 automatic column shift transmission. The interior is reportedly brand new, featuring a custom cluster and dash. Buyers can also expect power steering, power front disc brakes, and absolutely no roll cage or racing seats. In case the internet isn’t a good enough source to trust, interested prospect would find it in Simi Valley, California.
It is simply a comfortable street cruiser wearing a massive rear wing, rocking Winger Warrior swagger like history comes with unilaterally revokable terms and conditions. Ultimately, this confusing machine is described as a true one-of-a-kind project and a guaranteed head turner. I’m fairly certain that whoever put this together deserves an award – if not for determination, then for originality.
It will undoubtedly turn heads everywhere it goes, mostly because confused onlookers will be desperately trying to identify it. This rolling “hold my beer” paradox proves that with enough fiberglass, red paint, and wild imagination, anything is completely possible. Whether it should be possible is an entirely different debate. One that doesn’t come cheap at all.
Via // Facebook Marketplace

The BMW M6 Convertible Now Costs Virtually Nothing in the States
14 photos
Photo: Cars&Bids
Mind you, this is still a great open-top grand tourer with a focus on performance, which has aged like fine wine, packs plenty of features, and has a great V8 engine under the hood.
The last generation preceded the M8, and was offered in three body styles, just like its successor, These included the F13 Coupe, the F12 Convertible, and the F06 Gran Coupe, all of which had a front-engine and rear-wheel drive layout, and used the same 4.4-liter V8 engine with twin turbos, mated to a six-speed manual transmission or a seven-speed dual-clutch automatic transmission.
The 2012 BMW M6 Convertible pictured in the gallery had 553 horsepower (560 ps/412 kW) to play with and 502 pound-feet (680 Nm) of torque, and everything is channeled to the (rear) wheels through a dual-clutch seven-speed automatic transmission. From 0 to 60 mph (0 to 97 kph), it needed just 4.3 seconds officially, and its top speed was 155 mph (250 kph). The latter number increased to 190 mph (305 kph) on cars equipped with the optional M Driver’s Pack.
According to the spec sheet, this machine features the Driver Assistance Package and the Executive Package. It rides on 20-inch wheels (343M), has a power-retractable ragtop, full Merino leather upholstery, a heated steering wheel, and carbon fiber trim. There are no notable modifications mentioned in the ad, and there is nothing to be worried about when it comes to the known issues.
Photo: Cars&Bids That’s because this BMW M6 Convertible has scratches on the wheels, a cracked door mirror casing on the right side, wear on the headlight lenses, chips and scratches on the outside, some of which have been touched up, and some wear on the seats and interior surfaces. The dealer reported that the rear bumper has been repainted, and there is a mileage inconsistency in September 2016, though the vendor noted it “a clerical error,” the ad shows.
At the time of cataloging, this open-top, V8-powered grand tourer had 60,700 miles (97,700 km) on the clock. The car features a San Marino Blue Metallic paint finish, a black cockpit, and has a clean Texas title, being located in Lewisville, TX, prior to the sale that we will get to in a few moments.
It had it engine oil and filter changed, the brake fluid flushed, and the cabin air filter replaced / cleaned at 55,864 miles (89,953 km), in April of 2023, and in March 2022, this ride had its four tires replaced, an alignment performed, the engine oil and filter changed, and the cabin air filter replaced / cleaned, at 52,655 miles (84,740 km).
The vendor, a used car dealer, reportedly bought this BMW M6 Convertible in September 2026, adding some 150 miles (240 km) since, and since they are in this game to make money, the listed it for grabs on Cars&Bids. The online auction ended on October 9, 2026, and when the gavel hit the table, this machine ended up changing hands for $19,250. That’s basically nothing considered that this thing had an MSRP of roughly $114,000 back in the day.
Photo: Cars&Bids But was it a steal, or is this pretty much the usual selling price for the 2012 model year BMW M6 Convertible? The answer leans on the latter, because on average, this model now fetched between $16,000 and close to $30,000. The latter sum is obviously reserved for nicely-maintained examples that have not seen that much action over the years. Used car dealers usually sell it between $24,000 and $28,000, and the high-mileage units that are not exactly top notch fetch less than $20,000 in today’s used car market.
Nevertheless, paying less than $20K for what is still a great driver’s car and an awesome daily that features a V8 engine paired with a smooth-shifting automatic transmission that delivers everything to the rear axle is something to write home about in our book, because this remains a fantastic ride if properly maintained. And speaking of that, it’s not exactly reliable, as there are plenty of things that can go wrong, especially with the powertrain, and some electrical goodies.
Therefore, one should be ready to cough out a lot of money on the maintenance, and this is pretty much the reason for the often low selling price of these things. Nevertheless, the FX-generation of the BMW M6 remains a lot of car for the money, and let’s be honest, it has aged like fine wine, hasn’t it? This applies to all body styles, but to me, the two-door coupe looks absolutely perfect, and so does the four-door sedan, and I have to admit that I’m not necessarily a fan of the convertible variant.
If you want to check out the pictured 2012 BMW M6 Convertible in more detail, then you can do so here , though don’t forget to tell us if you would have paid almost $20K on this example before you click that link.

Intel-GPU-D-Series-Accelerator Hero
Amid a flurry of product announcements and updates at this year’s Open Compute Project Global Summit, Intel is at the show to deliver an update on Crescent Island, the company’s forthcoming AI inference GPU. After outlining the chip’s architecture back at Hot Chips 2026, the company is offering a short update on the product today, outlining some of the chip’s final performance specifications along with giving the cards based on it a proper name. Going forward, Crescent Island will be sold as part of Intel’s GPU D-Series.
Hot Chips 2026 Intel Crescent Island Slide 19 LPDDR 5x Open
Speeds and Feeds: Crescent Island Nears Release
As a brief refresher, Crescent Intel’s is first commercial AI-focused data center GPU since Ponte Vecchio in 2021. With two of Ponte’s successors canceled over the last few years – Rialto Bridge in 2023 and then Falcon Shores in 2025 – Intel announced Crescent Island at least year’s OCP Global Summit as an interim product to target the AI inference market with a heavily cost and power-optimized part. The resulting chip is not meant to be on the same performance level as flagship chips such as NVIDIA’s Blackwell Ultra or AMD’s MI455X, but then it will be a lot smaller and cheaper as well.
Most recently, Intel delivered an update on Crescent Island back in August , where the company offered a fairly detailed look at the architecture behind the chip. Based on an enhanced version of their Xe3 GPU architecture that they are calling Xe3P, Crescent Island heavily fortifies the architecture with a far larger number of XMX matrix engines, and a far larger LPDDR5X memory subsystem to keep those matrix blocks fed. In effect, Intel is banking on a massive matrix math version of Xe3 that is backed by a large LPDDR5X memory pool of up to 480GB being able to compete favorably with other inference accelerators on the market today.
Hot Chips 2026 Intel Crescent Island Slide 8 Crescent Island Architecture
For this year’s OCP Global Summit, in turn, Intel is finally publicly locking down some of the specifications for the forthcoming accelerator. In particular, we finally have the theoretical total compute and total memory bandwidth figures for the first card based on Crescent Island, which gives us enough information to paint a fairly detailed look at how the chip is configured.
Intel GPU D-Series Specifications
 | Intel GPU D270
Xe Cores | 32
XMX Engines | 256
GPU Clockspeed | ~2.5GHz
Peak Matrix Throughput (FP8) | 1.3 PFLOPS
Peak Vector Throughput (FP64) | 10.2 TFLOPS
Memory (Max) | 480GB LPDDR5X (ODMs) 160GB LPDDR5X (Intel)
Memory Bandwidth | 1.5TB/sec (~9375Mbps x 1280-bits)
ECC | Yes
L2 Cache | 32MB
I/O | PCIe Gen5 x16
TDP | 350W
Form Factor | PCIe CEM (Air Cooled)
Architecture | Xe3P
GPU | Crescent Island
In regards to performance, Intel is touting 1.3 PFLOPs of FP8 matrix performance. With 256 XMX matrix engines on the chip itself, this gives us a clockspeed of roughly 2.5GHz.
As for memory bandwidth, the flagship card will offer 1.5TB/second of memory bandwidth, which comes courtesy of its hefty 20 chip, 80 channel LPDDR5X memory bus, with the memory clocked at roughly 9375MT/second.
While Intel had previously discussed the architecture of the chip, the total performance and bandwidth had been up in the air. In practice, these figures are very close to what most of the industry has been expecting for the accelerator given current LPDDR5X memory speeds as well as the kind of clockspeeds that similar accelerator architectures have been hitting. In that respect Intel is delivering right in the neighborhood of where they should be – meaning that Crescent Island is not surpassing expectations, but it is not failing to meet them, either.
As to whether 1.3 PFLOPs of FP8 will be sufficient for Intel’s target market of data center inference operations, that remains to be seen. For comparison’s sake, AMD’s similar PCIe CEM form factor MI350P accelerator can offer a theoretical peak of 2.3 PFLOPs of dense FP8 matrix math; so a Crescent Island card comes in some 40% lower. With that said, comparing different architectures based on theoretical throughput alone rarely pans out in the real world, so a lot of the GPU’s competitiveness is going to hinge on its overall architectural efficiency compared to AMD’s CDNA 4 architecture. Especially if Intel can do meaningfully better in prefill, which is traditionally where GPU-based architectures bottleneck in data center-scale workloads.
Hot Chips 2026 Intel Crescent Island Slide 3 Accelerator Portfolio for Agentic AI
The bigger differentiator there will likely be power and cooling. The flagship Crescent Island card is a 350 Watt card that can be air cooled, whereas MI350P’s highest performance configuration is 600 Watts. Even more so than inference performance, Intel has been touting Crescent Island’s efficiency on a performance-per-watt basis, so for Intel’s intended market the card does not necessarily need to be the fastest option, so long as it is a more power efficient option than other PCIe cards.
Finally, Intel has once again confirmed that we will see multiple memory configurations with Crescent Island cards. The company’s own card will ship with 160GB of LPDDR5X memory (20x8GB chips). However, ODM partners will be able to offer versions with up to 480GB of memory, an extreme amount of memory enabled by 24GB LPDDR5X chips and a far larger capacity than any other PCIe form factor accelerator announced thus far.
Intel GPU D-Series: Crescent Island Gets a Name
Meanwhile, Crescent Island cards are finally getting a series name. For Intel’s new series of data center AI inference cards the company is launching a new brand name for them: the Intel GPU D-Series.
Intel-GPU-D-Series-Accelerator-Render
The first (and so far, only) card in the series is the GPU D270, pictured above. The image, a render, does not reveal anything we do not already know about Intel’s target market for the cards. But it does reinforce that this is a double-wide PCIe card meant to go into traditional PCIe-based data center servers.
Notably, Intel is not keeping the Data Center GPU Max (or Flex ) branding here, which is what Intel has used for its Ponte Vecchio and Arctic Sound-based PCIe cards. Despite being aimed at much of the same HPC market as the Data Center GPU Max family (and effectively its successor), the GPU D-series is its own product through and through.
The D-series suffix does invite some comparisons to another Intel D-named product, the Xeon D lineup. However, those chips were aimed at networking and edge devices, whereas the 350 Watt GPU D270 is very much a data center part. Plus the Xeon D brand was effectively put on a retirement glide path in 2025 with the launch of the Xeon 6 SoC series of chips (Granite Rapids-D), which are replacing Xeon D in that market. So the best way to interpret the new name is that Intel is starting anew, at least as far as GPU hardware goes.
Final Words
Wrapping things up, with today’s announcement Intel is slowly laying the remaining groundwork for the full launch of the GPU D-series. At this point the company has all but fully revealed its specifications and theoretical performance – now it is just a matter of when it will ship, and how much Intel will charge for it.
But the answers to those questions will have to wait for another day. For now, Intel is confirming that they are sampling cards to customers. However the company has not yet announced a launch date for the cards, or even confirmed that they will launch in what remains of this year. So AI server vendors looking for an alternative for PCIe inference cards will have to look towards 2027 for the release of Intel’s GPU D-series.

Picture a Europe that is burning through approximately 1 billion euros every single day on trade deficits with the People's Republic of China. This isn't a hypothetical scenario, but the harsh reality of an increasingly uncompetitive continent. Instead of learning a thing or two from Chinese players, the suits in Brussels have decided to protect European economies and established automakers from cheaper and more tech-heavy Chinese hybrid imports.
Last year alone, the deficit scaled to a staggering 360 billion euros. Surging vehicle shipments from Chinese manufacturers turned a macroeconomic headache into a crisis situation, and Chinese automakers are all too happy to aggressively ramp up exports in order to escape a brutal sales slump at home.
The European Union originally provided them with an inviting open door, only to then slap aggressive tariffs on Chinese battery-electric vehicles in 2024. That levy wasn't enough to fend off these newcomers, leaving the door open for hybrids. China exploited the regulatory oversight, capturing roughly a quarter of the entire hybrid market in Europe by August 2026.
Total vehicle imports, meanwhile, jumped nearly three-quarters through August 2026. Said information comes from Dataforce, cited by the peeps at Bloomberg, with the latter also reporting that established automaker watched their market share evaporate in thin air. Mercedes, for example, experienced an 8 percent drop during the third quarter of the current year.
The Volkswagen Group has it rough as well, slashing its profit forecast mere weeks after BMW issued a similar warning. In light of this pressure, both Germany and France lost patience. Ahead of emergency trade negotiations, Berlin and Paris demanded that Brussels expand its retaliatory arsenal. They even suggested that the European bloc consider severing trade ties with bad actors launching trade wars.
Photo: MG Both Germany and France further pressed for aggressive subsidy probes into foreign chemicals and plastics, which goes to show how desperate both economies are. In any case, that kind of political muscle does not go unnoticed. EU trade chief Maros Sefcovic met Chinese commerce minister Wang Wentao in Beijing, and their resulting agreement has produced a strict volume framework affecting Chinese hybrid vehicle imports.
For the initial 12 months, China would be hit by a 350,000-vehicle ceiling. Across a four-year enforcement window, the ceiling is planned to climb by 6 percent annually. Both trading blocs committed to respecting the WTO's guidelines throughout the process. As part of this deal, members of the European Economic Area, developing WTO members, Ukraine, and Kenya, specifically markets with negligible import shares, will be exempt.
This policy drags in self-charging hybrids and plug-in setups. In its current form, the document does not clarify whether shipments breaching the cap face outright border bans or steep punitive tariffs. Beijing, for its part, did not hand over such concessions without something to gain for itself.
China agreed to strip tariffs from select automotive parts while cutting duties in half for olive oil, ice cream, and shoes, which is a terribly interesting combo when you think about it. Also temporary, this package is worth approximately 4 billion euros. Bloomberg reports the EU's safeguard measure could take effect as soon as December 1, 2026.
Sefcovic is scheduled to return to Beijing early next year to audit early results. Whether a paper wall of 350,000 hybrids plus 6 percent yearly increases can halt a runaway freight train remains an open question, though.
While this measure protects both European economies and legacy automakers, it does not fix what everyone and their dog currently detests about the Volkswagen Group and similar automakers. Think high prices, very questionable quality, increasingly poor aftersales services, and other compounding issues that made them lose European customers to Chinese brands in the first place.

The latest iteration of Lockheed Martin’s PAC-3 family of missile interceptors is designed to bring extreme agility to bear against a diverse array of missile threats, Defense News learned.
The defense giant unveiled the PAC-3 Edge this Friday and debuted it at the Association of the U.S. Army’s annual meeting in Washington, D.C., today.
“This missile is capable of being launched from the traditional M903 launcher. It’s capable of being launched from the containerized launchers that are being sought after domestically and internationally, as well as our HIMARS FLEX, which is the offense and defense configuration of our traditional HIMARS vehicle,” Jason Reynolds, vice president and general manager of Lockheed Martin Missiles and Fire Control Integrated Air and Missile Defense, told Defense News.
Lockheed in January announced a seven-year framework agreement to increase annual PAC-3 interceptor production from approximately 600 to 2,000.
Designed to defend against hypersonic and advanced missile threats, the unveiling of the PAC-3 Edge comes as the U.S. military’s reliance on costly interceptors against cheap munitions, particularly those deployed by Iran during Operation Epic Fury, has come under increased scrutiny over the past eight months.
The new PAC-3 Edge missile builds on the foundations of the PAC-3 MSE, Lockheed’s baseline missile, and pushes its abilities farther.
The Edge system is longer and features a larger diameter, increasing its range.
“It also goes higher in altitude and has more agility. It has attitude control motors, which are located near the front of the missile and basically divert the missile in flight,” Reynolds explained. “This has additional attitude control motors that give it additional agility.”
While the PAC-3 MSE uses a two-pulse solid rocket motor to speedily approach moving targets, the new system has multi-pulse motor designed by Northrop Grumman.
“It has a third pulse to the motor, so that means the motor will fire three times during its flight, giving it additional agility to kill the target,” Reynolds said.
The weapon is designed not only for unprecedented maneuverability but to be easily integrated with both present and future missile defense networks. It is compatible with Northrop’s Integrated Battle Command System, or IBCS, a command-and-control network the Army uses to mesh air and missile defense sensors into a central hub.
The company intends to begin testing the PAC-3 Edge in 2027 and have it ready to deploy by 2031, although Lockheed aims to have it ready earlier, Reynolds added.
“The U.S. Army’s timeline is 2031. We, Lockheed Martin, are trying to pull that in and deliver this capability sooner, so around the turn of the decade,” he said.

Zita Ballinger Fletcher previously served as editor of Military History Quarterly and Vietnam magazines and as the historian of the U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration. She holds an M.A. with distinction in military history.

source_document.body:
KYIV, Ukraine — Ukraine is scrambling to secure enough Patriot interceptors to stop Russian ballistic missiles this winter, piecing together allied stockpile transfers , new production agreements and a homegrown interceptor program as quickly as possible before the cold sets in.
The push comes as the world runs short on the weapons Ukraine needs most. U.S. forces in Europe face a “beyond critical” shortage of Patriot interceptors after stocks were moved to the Middle East for the Iran war , a NATO official said in August.
Ukraine is also bracing for another winter of Russian strikes on its energy grid, a campaign that increasingly relies on jet-powered Shahed drones too fast for most of the cheap interceptor drones Ukraine has used to stop older models.
“Russia uses almost only jet-powered Shaheds to attack Kyiv because the interceptors that we were using in the past against older generations of drones had an interception rate of around 90%,” a manager at Ukrainian interceptor developer Grim Tech told Defense News last month.
The faster drones force Ukraine to expend scarce and expensive missiles just as it tries to conserve Patriot ammunition for ballistic threats — the only reliable option against Russia’s even harder-to-stop ballistic missiles, according to Ukrainian officials.
“Ballistic missiles are especially difficult to deal with,” President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said after a massive aerial barrage on Wednesday night saw Russia fire 70 missiles, many of them ballistic, and waves of Shahed drones at Kyiv and 12 other regions.
Soldiers downed 39 of the 48 cruise missiles but only five ballistic missiles, according to Ukraine’s air force . At least 32 people were killed in the attacks, and over 100 were injured, Zelenskyy wrote on Telegram .
Civilian casualties in Ukraine have risen monthly throughout most of 2026. U.N. monitors verified 372 civilians killed and 2,349 injured in August, second only to July, with long-range missiles and drones causing 47% of the toll.
Kyiv is assembling a patchwork of antiballistic air defense solutions, each piece on a different clock: Rounds transferred from allied stocks for this winter, imported systems and licensed production that will begin to matter over the next several years, and Freyja, a Ukrainian-European interceptor still in development.
Stockpile swaps
The fastest fix depends on allies sharing existing stockpiles, a request Defense Minister Yevhen Khmara put forward at his first Ukraine Defense Contact Group meeting with allies on Sept. 8.
Kyiv has signed contracts for roughly 1,000 Patriot missiles in recent months, but most will not ship for years, Khmara said.
He asked partners for 300 interceptors from their stockpiles now, offering newer missiles from those contracts as replacements.
“The situation with ballistics is much more difficult. And that difficulty is precisely down to the lack of Patriot missiles,” he told allies.
Germany answered Khmara’s call by promising an undisclosed number of PAC-2 interceptors from Bundeswehr stocks.
Britain committed £100 million through NATO’s Prioritised Ukraine Requirements List (PURL) for Patriot missiles and other air-defense equipment intended to arrive before winter, according to the British government .
But the United States did not include Patriot missiles in the nearly $400 million in expiring Ukraine Security Assistance Initiative money it moved to obligate before the fiscal year ended, a source familiar with the package told Reuters .
Surging production of existing antiballistic interceptors
“Ukraine is ready not only to produce ballistic missile interceptors for its own needs, but also to strengthen the United States and its allies through joint production,” Zelenskyy wrote on X after a recent meeting with a U.S. congressional delegation in Kyiv.
Both Europe and the U.S. are in talks with Ukraine to begin ramping up joint manufacturing initiatives for both the Patriot missile system and the Franco-Italian Aster 30.
Zelenskyy said Sept. 25 that U.S. President Donald Trump made a final political decision to grant Ukraine licenses to produce Patriot missiles. But Washington and manufacturers have not publicly identified the variant, Ukraine’s workshare, production site or first-delivery date.
Lockheed Martin said it aims to raise its own annual PAC-3 MSE capacity from roughly 600 missiles to 2,000 by 2030, while a $14.7 billion Boeing contract would triple production of the interceptor’s seeker.
Germany is scheduled to begin PAC-2 GEM-T production , and Berlin has separately asked Washington and Lockheed Martin to permit PAC-3 MSE production in Germany, but that proposal remains unresolved.
France and Italy agreed in a joint declaration in July to authorize licensed production of Aster 30 interceptors in Ukraine before the end of 2026, along with providing Kyiv with four SAMP/T NG systems — becoming their first combat user.
France also committed two interim SAMP/T complexes, a GF300 radar before year’s end and progressive SAMP/T NG deployment beginning in 2027.
The sovereignty bet: Freyja
Ukraine and Europe are looking to a new weapon called “Frejya” as a longer-term solution.
Freyja is a Ukrainian-designed ballistic interceptor built around Fire Point’s FP-7.X missile, including an interceptor, launcher, radar and command-and-control network.
It’s priced at roughly $1 million per round, about one-quarter of the cost of a PAC-3 MSE, and designed to plug into NATO-standard radars and command posts already in the field.
The FP-7.X flew for the first time in early June and is built to kill ballistic targets at roughly 15 miles up using a high-explosive fragmentation warhead rather than the PAC-3’s hit-to-kill collision — which may come in later versions — at a target price of approximately $700,000 per interceptor, or roughly one-fifth the price of a PAC-3.
The company says it will build three interceptors a day starting in August. Zelenskyy wants the system up and running within a year, and the coalition is targeting its first real ballistic intercept for the end of 2027.
Zelenskyy launched the initiative with nine European countries in Paris in July — and the effort is still growing.
Poland joined the group on Sept. 17, a week after Canadian PM Mark Carney told Zelenskyy that Ottawa would contribute its technologies to Freyja along with providing Kyiv with a broader package that includes C$350 million in interceptors.
The EU is separately weighing direct funding for the program on top of national contributions, according to Militarnyi .

Katie Livingstone is the Ukraine correspondent for Defense News and Military Times. Based in Kyiv, she has covered Russia's full-scale invasion since its first days. She is a former Fulbright fellow whose award-winning work has appeared in outlets across Europe and the U.S.

Other Components
Marvell Structera X 3506
CXL has seen a massive surge recently, and Marvell announced its second-generation Structera X CXL memory expanders, adding CXL 3.2 support, PCIe Gen6 connectivity, and increasing memory channels from four to six. For hyperscalers running DDR4 and lower-speed DDR5 reclamation projects, that means the DDR4 version can support up to 18 DDR4 RDIMMs.
Marvell Structera X 3406 and 3506 CXL 3.2 Memory Expanders
Patrick gave us the decoder for the models:
CXL 3 support is indicated by the first digit 3, just as the 2 in last year’s 2404 and 2504 marked CXL 2.0.
5 or 4, is the DDR generation
The trailing two digits are the memory channel count.
Structera X 3406 is therefore a CXL 3 DDR4 part with six channels, while the 3506 is the CXL 3 DDR5 part, also at six channels. This announcement covers only the Structera X memory expansion line, not the Structera A near-memory compute controller that Marvell showed us last year. Still, CXL is focused on optimizing either bandwidth per core (since CXL bandwidth is in addition to native DDR bandwidth) and also capacity expansion.
Marvell CXL Addresses Memory-intensive Applications Bandwidth / core High-bandwidth ML/AI inference DLRM Maximize memory bandwidth
PCIe Gen6 infrastructure and CXL 3.2 means we get roughly twice the bandwidth over the link, so that is how Marvell is adding more bandwidth from more memory channels.
Marvell New: CXL 3.2 Memory Expander CPU Structera X 3406/3506 CPU … Memory-expansion controllers 2x
Both new controllers stay on Marvell’s 5nm process and have LZ4 compression. Compression means the installed memory is storing more than the physical DRAM capacity. In this generation, Marvell is ensuring that the LZ4 can keep up with the interface so it is not a bottleneck. Here is the comparison table with key specs:
Marvell CXL Expander Product Overview Category DDR4 – Stuctera X 2404 DDR5 – Stuctera X
Structera X 3506 pairs six DDR5 channels with LZ4 compression at 250GB/s, while the 3406 runs DDR4 with six channels at 1600MT/s and 3DPC. That lets the DDR4 part take 18 DIMMs for up to 9TB per controller, and the DDR5 3506 takes 12 DIMMs for up to 6TB. CXL 3.2 lets up to four hosts share pooled memory, with up to 256GB/s of host bandwidth, double the prior generation’s 128GB/s.
Marvell Page Compressibility With Structera X Expander Frequency of obtaining given compression ratio by data’s
We have known that memory pages have varying levels of compressibility, and Marvell gave us some data on that.
Final Words
We covered the first-generation Structera X and Structera A when we visited Marvell’s labs last year, including how line-rate LZ4 compression makes attached memory roughly half as costly per gigabyte. That hands-on look explains why CXL expanders are attractive as AI demand tightens DRAM supply and pushes DDR5 prices up .
For hyperscalers, this seems like a better version of the 2000 series. Unlike many of Marvell’s competitors who are moving to four channels in their CXL 3.x generation, six channels put 50% more DRAM behind a single controller.

The US electric vehicle market delivered its strongest performance in a year in the third quarter. Here are the top 10 most popular so far this year.
US electric vehicle sales bounce back in Q3 2026
The “reset phase” following the expiration of the federal $7,500 tax credit last September is largely behind us, according to Stephanie Valdez Streaty, director of insights at Cox Automotive.
A total of 266,630 electric vehicles were sold in the US in Q3, Kelley Blue Book estimates, up 7.7% from the second quarter, and the highest since EV sales peaked in Q3 2025.
While EV sales were down 38.6% from a year ago, it was due to the tax credit expiring at the end of Q3 2025, which led to a rush of buyers before the quarter ended.

Beyond that, the third-quarter results suggest the market is finding its footing again and continuing to recover from the expected correction. Electric vehicles accounted for 6.5% of all new car sales in the third quarter, up from 5.8% in Q2, but still far from the over 10% achieved in Q3 2025.
2027 Toyota bZ (Source: Toyota)
Although most automakers posted lower EV volume than the year prior when the credit expired, several brands bucked the trend.
Toyota and Lexus continued leading the growth, with EV sales surging 328% and 442% from the prior year.
2026 Subaru Trailseeker (Source: Subaru)
Rivian delivered a strong third quarter, with sales jumping 46%, while Subaru posted 31% growth driven by its trio of new electric SUVs.
The top 10 best-selling EVs through Q3 2026
Through Q3, Tesla remains the dominant leader, with the Tesla Model Y and Model 3 holding the No. 1 and No. 2 spots.

Acting Secretary of the Army Adam Telle speaks during the Opening Ceremony of the 2026 Association of the United States Army. (U.S. Army photo by Christopher Kaufmann)
WASHINGTON — Acting Army Secretary Adam Telle today announced the service will hold an event aimed at finding weak spots in the service’s supply chain, which the service is calling a “manufacturing rodeo.”
“We need to make the things we need here in America, and to keep making them when demand surges. That’s why I’m announcing today that the US Army is going to do something we’ve never done before,” Telle said today at the annual AUSA conference, marking his largest address to soldiers and industry since taking on the acting secretary role.
“Early next year, we will conduct what I’m calling a manufacturing rodeo, a race between our industrial base partners.”
Telle did not divulge many details about the upcoming event, but said since the Army has invested “a lot in our organic industrial base ,” the service will now hold a competition of sorts between industry where they will “strain” and “stress test” the supply chain to “see where it breaks.”
“The magic is that this is an early indicator that we’re acquiring a new system of seamless, frictionless symbiosis between the Army and American commercial excellence,” Telle said. “We built those muscles in World War II, but we haven’t flexed them since the Cold War, and as I said, the script has flipped. Take a basic attack drone. We need to be able to make millions of these. It may look simple, but it’s a flying supply chain we don’t control enough of.”
Though Telle said the Army is focused on modernization efforts such as bolstering its supply chain, he also wants to put an increased emphasis on getting “back to the basics.”
“I’m going to take it back to the basics, back to the dirt that lies beneath that foundation, because government agencies are in such a race trying to one up each other on the path to technocratic superiority that we often blow right past the fundamentals,” Telle said. “We’re so eager to talk about how we’re playing with the shiniest, newest, most headline-worthy gadgets that we forget what we were trying to do in the first place.”
Getting back to the basics includes focusing on “controlling and securing land,” Telle said.
“[C]ontrolling land is fundamental to humanity. The Army does it better than anyone, and it’s on us, the people in this room, to keep it that way. Humanity’s connection to the land is biblical, and it even transcends faith.”
